text: A newborn can already pick out its mother's voice from another woman's, and will change the way it sucks to hear hers more often.
evidence: By sucking on a nonnutritive nipple in different ways, a newborn human could produce either its mother's voice or the voice of another female. Infants learned how to produce the mother's voice and produced it more often than the other voice.
check: Subjects were newborns (neonates), so the finding sits at the very start of age 0 (months 0-11). Abstract text confirmed via NCBI E-utilities (the PubMed page itself sits behind a browser check).

text: Toddlers aged 12 to 19 months average about 2,368 steps and 17 falls in every hour of free play.
evidence: Locomotor experience was immense: 12- to 19-month-olds averaged 2368 steps and fell 17 times/hour.
check: 12-19 months lies wholly inside the age-1 window (months 12-23). Figures from spontaneous free play (abstract: 'natural infant locomotion derived from spontaneous activity during free play'); US sample, New York University lab. Text confirmed via NCBI E-utilities PMC record.

text: By 30 months, most toddlers say about 50 words and join two together with an action, like “doggie run”.
evidence: Says about 50 words Says two or more words together, with one action word, like “Doggie run”
check: 30 months is inside age 2 (months 24-35). The two quoted lines are consecutive bullets on the page. CDC defines milestones as what 'most children (75% or more) can do by a certain age'. US CDC guidance.

text: Most three-year-olds can keep a conversation going for two back-and-forth turns, and have started asking who, what, where and why.
evidence: Talks with you in conversation using at least two back-and-forth exchanges Asks “who,” “what,” “where,” or “why” questions, like “Where is mommy/daddy?”
check: Checklist 'by 3 years' = 36 months, start of age 3 (months 36-47). The two quoted lines are consecutive bullets on the page. CDC: milestones are what 'most children (75% or more) can do by a certain age'.

text: Around four, children typically pass the classic false-belief test, predicting that someone will look for a toy where they last saw it, not where it now is.

source.label: Baillargeon, Scott & He, Trends in Cognitive Sciences, 2010

evidence: Beginning at about age 4, children typically answer correctly and point to the basket (where Sally falsely believes the toy is); in contrast, most 3-year-olds point to the box (where the toy actually is)
check: 'About age 4' = months 48-59, age 4. The review notes that infants show earlier signs on non-verbal tasks, so the text is limited to the classic (verbal) test. Text confirmed via NCBI E-utilities PMC record.

text: The grey matter of the brain's cortex reaches its greatest volume at about 5.9 years of age, according to charts built from 123,984 MRI scans.
evidence: showed an initial strong increase in GMV from mid-gestation onwards, peaking at 5.9 years (95% bootstrap confidence interval (CI) 5.8–6.1)
check: 5.9 years = about 71 months, inside the age-5 window (months 60-71); confidence interval 5.8-6.1 years. Scan count from the same paper: 'we aggregated 123,984 MRI scans, across more than 100 primary studies, from 101,457 human participants'. The paper defines GMV as 'total cortical grey matter volume (GMV)', separate from subcortical grey matter (sGMV), hence 'cortex'. Pooled international data.

text: In November 1960, six-year-old Ruby Bridges walked into William Frantz Elementary in New Orleans, escorted by U.S. Marshals, to desegregate the school.

source.label: National Women's History Museum, Ruby Bridges biography

evidence: An image of Ruby Bridges being escorted into William Frantz Elementary School by U.S. Marshals in November of 1960.
check: Born 8 Sep 1954 (NWHM: 'Ruby Bridges was born on September 8, 1954, to Abon and Lucille Bridges'; also NPS https://www.nps.gov/people/rubybridges.htm: 'Date of Birth: September 8, 1954'). Event: NWHM caption quoted in evidence, and 'It was not until November 14, 1960, that Louisiana schools began to desegregate'. NPS: 'She was the first African American child to desegregate William Frantz Elementary School.' 8 Sep 1954 -> 14 Nov 1960 = 6 years 2 months -> age 6.

text: In a US study of 100 children, 65% had had an imaginary companion at some point by the age of seven.
evidence: Overall, 65% of children up to the age of 7 had imaginary companions at some point during their lives.
check: 'Up to the age of 7' -> shown at age 7 (months 84-95). Sample: '100 children from this study were retested' three years after the preschool phase; University of Oregon, USA. Abstract confirmed via NCBI E-utilities.

text: Memories of age three fade slowly: children of five to seven recall most events they described then, while eight- and nine-year-olds recall under 40%.
evidence: Children aged 5, 6, and 7 remembered 60% or more of the early-life events. In contrast, children aged 8 and 9 years remembered fewer than 40% of the early-life events.
check: The under-40% figure applies to children aged 8 and 9 (months 96-119), so it is placed at age 8, where the drop first appears. Emory University, Atlanta, USA. Abstract confirmed via NCBI E-utilities.

text: In October 1828, nine-year-old Clara Wieck, later Clara Schumann, first played for the public, at Leipzig's Gewandhaus concert hall.
evidence: he introduced her to the public in a concert given by the pianist Caroline Perthaler from Graz, in the Leipziger Gewandhaus on October 20th, 1828.
check: Born 13 September 1819 (same page: 'Clara Wieck was born on September 13, 1819'). First public appearance 20 October 1828, within another pianist's concert (her first own concert followed on 8 November 1830, aged 11). 13 Sep 1819 -> 20 Oct 1828 = 9 years 1 month -> age 9.

text: The World Health Organization counts adolescence from 10 to 19. There are more adolescents alive than ever before: 1.3 billion, one in six people on Earth.

check: WHO defines adolescence as ages 10 to 19, so age 10 is its first year. Global figure (1.3 billion, one sixth of world population) as stated on the WHO health-topic page, current as fetched in Sept 2026; the page gives no reference year.

The Nobel page also states the age explicitly. Pen name 'Gul Makai' is on the same page.

text: Asked for their most meaningful songs, 1,891 people from around the world most often named ones released when they were about 17.

check: Release years of personally meaningful songs, relative to each participant's age, form an inverted U peaking at age 17 (1,891 participants, diverse countries). text: In April 2022 Japan lowered its age of adulthood from 20 to 18, the first change in roughly 140 years.
evidence: a law was enacted to revise a part of the Civil Code by reducing the age of majority in the Civil Code from 20 to 18 years old. … The first review of the age of majority in the approximately 140 years since the proclamation in 1876 … This revision will be effective from April 1, 2022.

text: The mind's raw speed at processing information peaks around 18 or 19, while vocabulary goes on growing until the late 60s or early 70s.
evidence: raw speed in processing information appears to peak around age 18 or 19, then immediately starts to decline. … the new data showed a later peak, in the late 60s or early 70s.

text: Sleep times drift later through the teens and reach their latest at around 20, a turning point proposed as a marker for the end of adolescence.

source.label: Nature News & Views on Roenneberg et al. (Current Biology), 2005

evidence: Children are typically early risers but start to sleep progressively later as they enter adolescence. They reach maximum lateness at around the age of 20, when the curve abruptly starts to decline. … the authors suggest, it is the point at which an individual's curve inverses that marks the end of adolescence.
check: Survey of 25,000 people aged 10-90 (Roenneberg et al., Curr. Biol. 2004), summarized in Nature 433:27 (2005): maximum lateness of sleep timing 'at around the age of 20'. The original paper is paywalled (cell.com returned 403), so the Nature summary is cited.

text: In 2025, young people in Finland left their parents' home at 21.4 years on average, the earliest in the EU, where the average was 26.3.

check: Eurostat news item of 2026-09-15, dataset yth_demo_030, reference year 2025: Finland 21.4 (lowest in EU), EU average 26.3. 21.4 falls in the age-21 window.

check: Born 1901-12-05 (NobelPrize.org facts, https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/1932/heisenberg/facts/); left for Helgoland on 1925-06-06 and worked there in June 1925 (APS, which also says 'then 23 years old'). text: Many people first notice around age 45 that they hold a page a little farther away to read it, as the lens of the eye slowly loses its flexibility.

text: Reading other people's emotions is a late-blooming skill: in a study of nearly 50,000 people it peaked in the 40s or 50s, long after processing speed and short-term memory.

text: Across 145 countries, well-being follows a U-shaped curve through adulthood, dipping to its lowest point in midlife, on average around age 48, then rising again.
